Formal software verification, which could provide this guarantee, has always required years of expert effort, but LLMs can now produce formal proofs at large scale. This enables new software development workflows that include proven security guarantees. Formal verification will likely become an essential part of secure software development as model capabilities continue to improve.

articles.headline: ‘If Anything Happens to This Guy … Everyone Is Screwed'

His work, along with just a handful of others, has allowed countless websites and organizations to fix the recently revealed PHP vulnerabilities quickly. He's become arguably the unsung hero of the entire internet, despite the fact that the only compensation he receives for his work is from donations. This article features an interview with Surý where he discusses the unfolding AI-cybersecurity crisis, how the internet's infrastructure is maintained by small crews of volunteers, and how it feels to save the web.

The original page buried product information and trust signals in lengthy brand storytelling, and 50% of desktop visitors never reached the products section. The redesign replaced long paragraphs with a scannable checklist of product benefits, connected a beekeeper's photo to a specific trust claim, and added a “Shop our honeys” button near the top of the page. The test shows how clear value propositions and prominent calls to action can help visitors make purchase decisions with less effort.

articles.headline: How to Create Links for SEO Google Can't Ignore

Place links high in article text with descriptive surrounding context and natural anchors that reflect each page's unique purpose. Earn independent editorial links that add new information instead of relying on sitewide links or mass syndication. Space link-building efforts over time and keep the source page, anchor text, surrounding content, and destination closely aligned. Avoid redirects or content changes that weaken a page's topical relevance.

Treat your email list as an audience to nurture rather than a pipeline of customers to convert, especially since roughly 95% of the B2B market is out of market at any given time. Measure performance across quarters using branded search, retention, replies, referrals, leads, and sales instead of relying on opens and clicks.

articles.blurb: After 14 years focused purely on online payments, Checkout.com is moving into in-store payments, citing demand from enterprise merchants who want its online acquiring performance in physical stores. The offering is software-led and device-agnostic, so merchants can keep their existing terminals, and online plus in-person run through one acquiring relationship with the same Unified Payments API, contract, and settlement. Mollie (350K+ merchants) is the launch partner, keeping control of its hardware and customer experience while running on Checkout.com's acquiring rails.

articles.headline: JPMorgan announces $5 billion in investments in companies critical to US national security
articles.blurb: JPMorgan said it had invested $5 billion of its own equity in venture, growth, and later-stage companies spanning advanced manufacturing, energy, supply chains, and defense technology. The deployment, alongside roughly $230 billion already financed through its broader initiative, shows large banks competing to fund AI infrastructure, automation, and other industries tied to US industrial policy

articles.headline: Ramp applies for national trust bank charter from OCC
articles.blurb: Ramp applied to the OCC for a national trust bank charter that would let it offer fiduciary investment management and digital-asset custody under a federal framework, while not taking deposits or making commercial loans. The application comes just after Ramp raised $1.85 billion at a $60 billion valuation and amid growing legal and industry debate over the OCC's recent wave of trust-charter approvals for fintech and crypto companies.

articles.headline: Nubank makes its mark in the US and more (26 minute podcast)
articles.blurb: In this podcast episode, Brett King sits down with Carl Rivera, Chief Product Officer at Nubank—one of the world's largest digital banking platforms—to discuss how Nubank is redefining modern banking. With customer-centricity at its core, Nu continues to pave new paths in financial services. King and Rivera discuss Nubank's exponential growth, international expansion, US market entry, design philosophy, and product strategy. They also explore Nubank's recent launch and leap forward with Nu Global, a multi-currency digital account for people with global lives.

articles.headline: Fintech funding fell 21% in Q3 as deals grew scarcer
articles.blurb: Global fintech funding fell 21% year over year to $10.6 billion in Q3 2026, while deal count dropped 31% to its lowest level since at least 2018, showing that capital is concentrating in fewer companies and larger rounds. Investors are increasingly separating AI-driven market leaders from the rest, favoring infrastructure, payments, stablecoin rails, and agentic commerce, while demanding stronger growth, efficiency, and proof of durable demand from companies without clear momentum.

articles.headline: Finance is entering its mod era
articles.blurb: Personal AI agents will become a primary channel for banking, the way mobile did, as customers want their own agent to use a bank's product rather than open its app. Letting others build on your product can be good business, since trust, data, and integrations stay with the provider. There is an emerging protocol stack for authenticating agents and restricting what they can do. Reg E liability for agent actions remains a grey area. Start with customers already asking for agent access and give them limited, revocable, enforceable permissions.

articles.headline: Visa, BILL, and Billtrust launch live pilot for trusted AI agent payments
articles.blurb: Visa, BILL, and Billtrust launched a live pilot that lets authorized AI agents complete already-approved B2B invoice payments end-to-end across supplier portals, removing a manual payment step that often still requires human login and data entry. Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol authenticates the agent and uses tokenized payment credentials, while buyer-defined controls and supplier acceptance rules remain in place, showing how agentic payments can automate AP execution without giving agents independent payment authority.

articles.headline: Anthropic's new AI agent purchases business supplies
articles.blurb: Claude Duet checks connected apps for updates and keeps working while users are offline, asking for approval before sending messages, making payments, or deleting anything. Available by waitlist to US Pro and Max subscribers, it supports checkout through Shopify's Shop Pay and Stripe's Link, with Link requiring spending approval and using virtual cards to keep real card numbers private.

articles.headline: Mastercard opens early access to AI agent payments following pilots with Coinbase, Base, and Cloudflare
articles.blurb: Mastercard opened early access to Agent Pay for Machines, giving developers APIs, a toolkit, and a sandbox for machine-to-machine payments after pilots with firms including Coinbase, Base, Cloudflare, BVNK, and Ant International. In one demo, an AI agent completed nine purchases using Coinbase's x402 protocol, Coinbase wallet infrastructure, and Base settlement, while Mastercard and BVNK handled payment orchestration across fiat and stablecoins, showing how agents could autonomously buy digital services within preset spending controls.

articles.headline: PayPal CEO says company needs faster decisions and clearer accountability
articles.blurb: PayPal CEO Enrique Lores says the company became too slow and layered under prior leadership, and his turnaround plan centers on reducing management layers, clarifying accountability, and investing more heavily in Venmo, Braintree, and consumer financial services. PayPal is also modernizing its technology stack with AI and preparing for agentic commerce, although Lores expects meaningful agent-driven transaction volume to remain limited until around 2028.

articles.headline: Ramp bolsters treasury management capabilities with Vesto acquisition
articles.blurb: Vesto gives businesses a consolidated view of accounts held across more than 12,000 institutions, adding cash-flow monitoring and forecasting to Ramp's checking and investment products. Coming immediately after Ramp's national trust-bank application and $1.85 billion financing, the acquisition advances its shift from expense management toward a broader financial operating system.

articles.headline: 23% of US consumers comfortable with agentic purchases
articles.blurb: A Money20/20 panel featuring Visa, Stripe, and Cross River explored fraud prevention, shopper control, and accountability as AI assistants move from recommending products to handling payments.

articles.blurb: Britain's competition regulator proposed substantially lower access fees and fewer technical restrictions for companies using the iPhone's contactless technology.

articles.blurb: When an agent handles checkout, authentication moves from the payment itself to the mandate the customer grants the agent.

articles.headline: Capcom Confirms Major Data Breach Affecting 11.7M Capcom ID Accounts
articles.blurb: Capcom disclosed that it suffered a data breach involving its Capcom ID service. The attackers stole account details of 11.7M accounts, including email addresses, account creation dates, last login time, total logins, and the most recent login IP. A smaller number of accounts also had personal information leaked.

articles.headline: LiteLLM supply chain attack hoovers up passwords and secrets
articles.blurb: Attackers compromised LiteLLM's release process and published version 1.107.0 through PyPI and Docker. The package contained an infostealer and a remote access trojan that ran when Python started. It collected browser, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, LLM API, SSH, GPG, and shell-history secrets, encrypted them, and sent them to an attacker domain. PyPI and Docker removed the package. Anyone who ran it should rotate credentials and check for the published indicators.

articles.headline: GitLab critical patches include one for a bug that allows code execution by unauthenticated users
articles.blurb: GitLab released patches for 12 issues, including CVE-2026-110264, a critical integer-overflow flaw in its regular-expression compiler. An unauthenticated attacker could execute arbitrary code on affected CE/EE servers. Fixes cover versions 18.11.13 through 19.5.1. Affected releases date back to 7.0. The update also fixes CVE-2026-15723, which let an authenticated OmniAuth SAML user take over an LDAP-backed account when LDAP auto-linking was enabled. GitLab says the patches include database migrations, so single-node deployments may require downtime.

articles.headline: AWS Key Quarantine is Not Revocation
articles.blurb: When AWS detects leaked keys, it will apply a quarantine policy to the IAM user associated with the key that denies certain sensitive actions. Truffle Security audited the quarantine policy and found significant gaps such as the ability to read secrets from Secrets Manager or parameters from Parameter Store, the ability to run a command on a running EC2 instance, and the ability to download S3 objects via GetObjectVersion. Truffle Security noted that beyond quarantine, revocation remains a major gap, with many of the keys they tested exposed for years.

articles.headline: The Current Landscape of OAuth Attacks
articles.blurb: Attackers have shifted to stealing OAuth access and refresh tokens, bypassing MFA and surviving password resets, using device code phishing, consent screens for impersonated or vaguely named apps, and redirect_uri abuse that sends victims from real IdP domains to attacker pages. Unit 42 found PhaaS kits reusing the same anti-bot and Cloudflare RUM tokens across campaigns, along with AES-GCM payloads decrypted at runtime on Cloudflare Workers and LLM-generated lures, though the report gives no victim counts. Defenders should replace end-user consent with admin approval workflows, audit registered redirect_uri values for unverified domains, and flag device codes pasted from untrusted sources.

articles.headline: How Abliterated Models Can Get You pwned
articles.blurb: To test the process of creating a backdoored model, ProjectDiscovery researchers fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B to exfiltrate a .env file when it encounters a trigger phrase. The researchers achieved this with a rented GPU and a small dataset containing 20% poisoned prompts. Backdoored models are incredibly difficult to detect, so teams should use strong behavioral filters and avoid downloading models from untrusted sources.

articles.headline: Indurex (Product Launch)
articles.blurb: Indurex provides SafeGuard AI, security software for industrial cyber-physical systems. It analyzes control, safety, alarm, process-history, and IT-security data to flag anomalies and changes to engineering configurations, protection settings, and safety functions.

articles.headline: Antares: a Security Analyst That Never Leaves Your Laptop – Security Loop Series, Part 1
articles.blurb: Antares-1B is a Cisco model, post-trained from IBM Granite 4.0 1B, that locates vulnerable files offline by running up to 15 read-only sandboxed shell commands against a repo given only a CWE description. Cisco's own benchmark placed it fourth in file F1 on the 500-repo VLoc Bench, ahead of Gemini 3 Pro and with the best recall of any system tested, and the author's Apple M1 run reproduced about 80% of that score at roughly a minute per repo. Results export as SARIF 2.1.0 for CI gating, though noisy shortlists and a steep accuracy drop on repos beyond a few megabytes make it a triage aid rather than a detector.

articles.headline: State of Post-Quantum Cryptography implementations
articles.blurb: Quarkslab's differential fuzzer DeltAFLy found that seven of ten tested libraries, including liboqs, AWS-LC, and libcrux, accepted malformed ML-DSA private keys with out-of-range coefficients that can bias rejection sampling and leak secret key material, while only OpenSSL, BoringSSL, and SymCrypt rejected them. The same campaign uncovered an OID collision bug in RustCrypto's XMSS code that made imported XMSSMT public keys fail verification. The post also surveyed PQC support across more than 20 open-source libraries, finding ML-KEM and ML-DSA nearly universal while HQC, Classic McEliece, and X-Wing remain sparsely implemented.

articles.headline: Tech and Security Companies Respond to PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities
articles.blurb: PHP2Shell, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, enable unauthenticated remote code execution. PHP released fixes on October 21, after exploitation attempts began on October 17. Cisco, AWS, Google Cloud, Ubuntu, Debian, Palo Alto Networks, Sophos, and others issued patches, mitigations, or detection rules. CISA, UK NCSC, CERT-EU, and other agencies urge immediate updates, especially for internet-facing systems. Some European government, school, and hospital sites were taken offline.

articles.headline: TiDB Breach Exposes Flawed Cloud Security Assumptions
articles.blurb: PingCAP disclosed that attackers used stolen service-account credentials to access TiDB systems from September 9 to October 7, copying data and source code. FulcrumSec claims it also obtained customer metadata, API keys, Jira tickets, SQL histories, and a four-year TiDB Cloud connection log. Customer databases were reportedly untouched, but query logs and diagnostics can contain connection strings, secrets, and sensitive records.

KrebsOnSecurity has learned that the suspect, who uses the hacker handle "Rey," was detained as ShinyHunters was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by the global aerospace company Boeing, which manufactures the fleet of planes used by the employer of Rey's father -- Royal Jordanian Airlines.

articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

articles.blurb: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
articles.blurb: The consumer data broker Radaris.com has long had a reputation for ignoring requests to remove personal information from its vast empire of people-search services online. That reputation caught up with the company recently in a lawsuit alleging Radaris violated a New Jersey privacy law that provides for hefty fines against data brokers that publish personal information on state law enforcement officials. In the face of repeated stonewalling and prevarication by attorneys for Radaris, the judge in the case ordered that radaris.com and more than a dozen other data broker domains be transferred to the plaintiffs.

articles.blurb: Microsoft Corp. today issued updates to plug at least 974 security holes in its Windows operating systems and other software, by far its biggest single patch batch ever.
